subject: Peak-to-commit mapping & short-lead GPU addendum
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <amercer@cerebellum.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:03 -0700
Subject: Observed peaks Q3 + renewal conversation

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for our annual renewal (Dec 1 effective date), we ran a short internal analysis and saw multiple short-duration peaks that breached our committed pool in August. I attached the CSV with timestamps and GPU-second counts — hope this helps.

For context: last three months we average 1.8m GPU-seconds/day but had three spikes where sustained tail latency-sensitive traffic required an extra 6-8 A100-equivalent GPUs for 30–90 minutes. Our ask: can we add a short-term burst or convert more of our burst usage into committed capacity without doubling our monthly commit? We're trying to avoid repeated outage-based fallbacks.

Attached: cerebellum_usage_peak_q3.csv [Attachment: cerebellum_usage_peak_q3.csv (CSV, 42KB)]

Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the rows.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of ML Platform, Cerebellum Labs
amercer@cerebellum.ai
From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <amercer@cerebellum.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 10:03:47 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed peaks Q3 + renewal conversation

Alex — thanks for sending this. I pulled the CSV and scanned the peaks. Broad proposal below; happy to review on a quick call.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Short-term: add a 30-day committed buffer of 8 A100-equivalent GPUs to cover observed peak windows and reduce fallback risk.
- Medium-term (renewal effective Dec 1): convert 60% of your historical burst consumption into a staged committed tranche with automated ramp triggers.
- Contract mechanics: we can add an amendment to your existing Dedicated SOW for the 30-day buffer (prorated) and include a path-to-commit credit if you convert within the renewal window.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Operations check: confirm procurement lead time for the extra GPUs (cc'ing Karthik and Ben).
2) Pricing: I will draft an amendment with a prorated cost for the 30-day buffer + an option to apply credit toward a Dec conversion.
3) Observability: Laura will set up a short dashboard that highlights exhaustion windows so we can show real-time impact during the buffer period.

I'll attach a working draft for Ops and the amendment skeleton once I hear back from Karthik on lead times.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: none]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 08:31:19 -0700
Subject: RE: Observed peaks Q3 + renewal conversation

Team — operational constraints and lead-time reality below. I pulled procurement and infra timelines; attaching a short kit of lead times.

Key notes:
- HW lead time: for air-gapped/dedicated A100-class nodes our typical procurement + rack-in takes 4–6 weeks if we secure immediate vendor slots. For prioritized tranches we can trim to ~3 weeks but there is a 15% expedite fee.
- Hot-standby approach: If Cerebellum wants immediate coverage while hardware arrives, we can temporarily allocate hosted burst capacity (cross-tenant) mapped to their routing policy with stricter data separation controls for the 30-day window. That reduces immediate SLA risk.
- Cost impact: a 30-day dedicated buffer of 8 A100-eq maps to $X/month prorated on the SOW; if customer converts to committed by Dec 1 we offer a credit equal to 40% of the prorated buffer cost toward the first three months of the new commit.

Action items I need from Sales:
- Connor: confirm whether Cerebellum prefers (A) expedited procurement for dedicated GPUs or (B) immediate hosted burst + deferred dedicated arrival.
- Laura: confirm observability dashboards we will expose to the customer during the buffer period (token-level latency and exhaustion alerts).

Attachments: procurement_lead_times.xlsx [Attachment: procurement_lead_times.xlsx (XLSX, 28KB)]

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Dedicated Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Alex Mercer <amercer@cerebellum.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Observed peaks Q3 + renewal conversation

Connor / Karthik / Laura —

Thanks — we've reviewed the choices internally with infra and procurement. We want to take option B: immediate hosted burst (to avoid the expedite fee) plus a pledged committed conversion path at renewal. Please prepare the 30-day buffer amendment (prorated) with the conversion credit language you outlined. Also put a DocuSign link for the amendment and add the HubSpot deal note (DL-2039).

We accept the observability plan — Laura, if you can share the dashboard and set up the first alert policy, we'll validate during the buffer.

Attachments to expect from you: redwood_proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (amendment skeleton) and a DocuSign link for signature.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — aiming to have the buffer active by Oct 5.

—Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of ML Platform, Cerebellum Labs
